headline: Fashion Design & Creative Direction - Training AI to understand my language | AI MOVER & SHAKER 2026 in Fashion by CHOICE DAO | Botika, Caimera, Flora & Lumoo Creative Partner

sections.position: Designer, Product Developer & Collection Manager @ Freelance
sections.bio:
I have spent my career working across fashion design, product development, and collection coordination, moving between creative vision and the realities of making. From bespoke and atelier work to private label, consulting, and large-scale collection development, I’ve always been drawn to the space where ideas are shaped, tested, and turned into product.

One of the strongest experiences in my career was my role on the Anglomania collection by Vivienne Westwood at Studio Cataldi Group, where I worked across design, development, and production in a fast-moving, high-level environment. That experience taught me how to protect creative vision while staying grounded in process, timing, cost, and execution. It strengthened a way of working that still defines me: creative, practical, collaborative, and deeply attentive to process.

Today, I also use AI as part of that process. Not as a replacement for experience, but as a tool to test, visualize, and refine ideas before  they move further. I’m particularly interested in collaborations that value strong direction, product understanding, and thoughtful  development, whether on the creative side, the product side, or both.

posts.text:
"CAIMERA & ME - THE CO-EVOLUTION"

A creative tool matures.
A designer matures.
And suddenly they meet each other halfway.

When I first started using Caimera, knitwear came with a warning. It simply wasn't a category the platform could render reliably.
At exactly the same time, I started revisiting my own knitwear archive.

So while Caimera was learning to understand stitches, texture and yarn...
...I was figuring out how to bring decades of knitwear design into the AI era.

Months later, the warning disappeared.
And somewhere along the way, I stopped making AI images and started directing editorials.

The sweater you're looking at is one of my own designs from years ago.
I'll share the original in the first comment.

Editorial styling: My archival knitwear design styled with Alexander McQueen's asymmetric deconstructed leather moto skirt (Spring/Summer 2023) and DSQUARED2's iconic Skate Moss boots (Fall/Winter 2011).

"CAN LUMOO REALLY DECONSTRUCT HAUTE COUTURE? I PUT IT TO THE TEST."

Rather than following the conventional workflow, I decided to reverse it.
Designers typically begin with sketches, flats or ghost garments before moving on to visualizations and campaigns.
My question was the opposite:
Could a finished Haute Couture runway look become the starting point instead?

I selected one of the most intricate looks from ZUHAIR MURAD's Paris Haute Couture collection and used Lumoo to isolate the garments from the runway image while preserving their silhouette, embellishment and overall design integrity.
Once extracted, those "ghost" garments became reusable design assets that could be placed into entirely new environments, creating a fresh editorial without rebuilding the garments from scratch.

For fashion designers, this opens interesting possibilities beyond visualization:
• Creating reusable garment libraries.
• Accelerating concept development.
• Exploring new styling and environments without rebuilding the garment each time.
• Extending the life of runway references within the creative process.

What impressed me most wasn't the realism.
It was the shift in workflow.
If a runway image can become a reusable design asset, what else have we been treating as the end of the process instead of the beginning?

"ADVERTISING CONCEPTS BUILT WITH FLORA"

People know me primarily for fashion.
What they don't always see is that the same creative thinking can extend far beyond it.
Over the past months, I've been exploring speculative campaigns across luxury, technology, lifestyle and consumer brands. 
Not to imitate existing advertising, but to ask a simple question:

What if these worlds collided?
What if Pirelli met luxury accessories?
What if Gaudí inspired Apple's product design?
What if Salvador Dalí reimagined Patek Philippe?
What if mythology shaped a Timberland campaign?
What if IKEA reassembled the Renaissance?
What if Durex asked rock legends a few uncomfortable questions? 
What if a box of BACI PERUGINA captured the electrifying chemistry of KISS?
What if Pashley Cycles were reimagined through the rebellious spirit of Vivienne Westwood?

Each project began as an idea and evolved into a complete visual concept inside FLORA, where I could develop, refine and art direct every campaign with speed and creative control.
For me, AI isn't the destination.
It's another creative medium - one that lets ideas move faster from imagination to execution.

I'm curious to know:
Which campaign would you most like to see become real?

Disclaimer: All projects featured are independent speculative concepts created for portfolio purposes. They are not affiliated with, endorsed by, or commissioned by the brands or individuals depicted.
